data.narrative: Completed Module 6 'Parallel Execution' learning about managing parallel workstreams with interface contracts, parallelism strategies (isolated branches vs shared context), synchronization points (end-only vs checkpoints), and detecting/fixing contract violations.

dimension_scores.observation: Created 7 interface contracts specifying exact data types, endpoint paths, error formats, and shared identifiers between parallel tickets
dimension_scores.evidence: artifacts/contracts-module-06.md contains 7 contracts covering database schema, ticket dependencies, and future integration points

dimension_scores.observation: Identified which tickets can run in parallel (Ticket A and C) and which cannot (Ticket A before B) based on hard dependencies
dimension_scores.evidence: module6_context.md explains Tickets A (provider availability API) and C (provider profile page) can run parallel, but A and B cannot run simultaneously

dimension_scores.observation: Chose isolated branches for parallelism strategy to prevent merge conflicts during development, chose checkpoint syncs to catch contract violations early rather than at big-bang integration
dimension_scores.evidence: Decisions documented: isolated branches (clean separation, no merge conflicts during dev) and checkpoint syncs (catch drift early, smaller fixes)

dimension_scores.observation: Contracts specify exact data types (UUID v4, ISO 8601 timestamps, decimal formats), field names, error cases, and shared identifiers with no ambiguity
dimension_scores.evidence: Contract 1 specifies datetime format as ISO 8601 with example, Contract 2 specifies error format as {error: message}

dimension_scores.observation: Detected contract violation (Unix timestamps vs ISO 8601) by systematically diffing agent output against contract, fixed by updating agent output, documented prevention strategies
dimension_scores.evidence: module6_break.md and module6_fix.md show violation detection, fix execution, and prevention strategies (shared types, contract tests, pre-merge checklist)

dimension_scores.observation: Verified end-to-end scenario (Sarah booking Mike's plumbing) tracing through both agents' code, confirmed response shapes match contracts, race condition handled by slot status validation
dimension_scores.evidence: module6_verification.md walks through complete scenario with actual JSON request/response examples

strengths: Created 7 comprehensive interface contracts with exact specifications
Chose isolated branches and checkpoint syncs to balance parallelism benefits with integration safety
Detected contract violation through systematic output vs contract comparison
Documented multiple prevention strategies for future violations
data.recommendation: Use parallel execution skills in real team settings - create interface contracts before starting parallel work, use contract tests in CI to catch violations automatically
